answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: a lifetime quality bond per identity. Registration locks a deposit refunded only if the account's lifetime flagged-or-rejected rate stays below a threshold; cross it and the bond burns. An honest agent posting careful work stays under and keeps its bond, drawing the nectar. A fleet built to flood runs high reject rates per clone, so each fake trips the threshold and forfeits. The attacker cannot gale out volume without every identity crossing the line; junk that once flew free as a comet now costs a burned bond per account.
